title: The unbounded exchange extends the bounded exchange
statement:
Let $\square$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$ and $g':X'\to X$. Use the derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and their full bounded below subcategories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Write $\iota_T:D^+(T_{\Et})\hookrightarrow D(T_{\Et})$ for the inclusions. For $K\in D^+(X_{\Et})$, the unbounded exchange $\Ex^{\mathrm{unb}}_{\square,\iota_XK}$ of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] at coefficient ring $\mathbf Z$ equals $\iota_{Y'}(\Ex^+_{\square,K})$, where $\Ex^+$ is the exchange of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange], under the canonical comparisons
$$u^{-1}\iota_V\cong\iota_Uu^{-1},\qquad Ru_{*,\mathrm{unb}}\iota_U\cong\iota_VRu_{*,+}\quad(u:U\to V)
$$
for the inverse images [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image] and direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. These are the comparisons that compute both direct images on the same bounded below injective representative.

For any commutative ring $\Lambda$ and any sheaf $F\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, place $F$ in degree zero. Under the canonical degree-zero identifications
$$
\mathcal H^0(g^{-1}Rf_*F[0])\cong g^{-1}f_*F,\qquad
\mathcal H^0(Rf'_*g'^{-1}F[0])\cong f'_*g'^{-1}F,
$$
the map $\mathcal H^0(\Ex^{\mathrm{unb},\Lambda}_{\square,F[0]})$ is the $\Lambda$-linear underived exchange. Here inverse image, direct image, and their adjunction are those on constant-ring module sheaves [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; the underived exchange is the mate of $g'^{-1}\varepsilon_f\circ\theta_\square$ in these module categories. Its underlying abelian morphism, through the canonical coefficient comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-underived-exchange], is the map of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. The identifications in this paragraph are induced by the augmentations into nonnegative injective resolutions. No assertion identifies the entire derived direct image of a sheaf with its ordinary direct image.

proof.text: Apply the unbounded adjunction Hom equivalence and its triangle identity to deduce the corresponding counit comparison. The exact derived square is the image of the bounded square under inclusion, by the composition and natural-isomorphism comparison formulas for exact functors. The bounded mate satisfies derivedBaseChangeMapPlus_fac_app, hence equals the bounded exchange by its extensionality theorem. Expanding the unbounded mate and using naturality together with these unit, square, and counit comparisons proves the displayed conjugation formula, for every abelian coefficient category satisfying the stated hypotheses.

proof.text: Identify the generic bounded base-change construction with the etale bounded exchange using their common derived-unit factorization and uniqueness. Apply rightDerivedBaseChange_zero_unit to the underived square mate. Expand rightDerivedBaseChange_app and cancel the degree-zero comparison isomorphisms to obtain the bounded exchange formula with the fixed homology endpoints. Apply the bounded/unbounded comparison from the previous step to F[0]. Naturality of the direct-image comparison with the inverse-image single-object isomorphism identifies its target endpoint; naturality of the exact-functor homology isomorphism identifies its source endpoint. Cancellation of comparison isomorphisms gives exactly exchangeSourceZeroIso and exchangeTargetZeroIso and the first degree-zero equality.
